`spec.md` and `acceptance.md` written at the repo root and copied into this run's stage outputs (`.bridza/pipelines/engineering/00000123-…/spec/outputs/`). The root pair replaced the stale #112 tag-colour spec.

**What the spec commits to** — one conversation per task, on its own `Chat` tab, that keeps working after every stage is `done`:

- Each message runs the picked agent in the task's worktree and commits **one commit per turn, appended**. That's the one real departure from `runStage`, which soft-resets and *replaces* a stage's commit — which is exactly why "improvise after the flow" can't be a stage re-run today without rewriting the record of what that stage did.
- `chat` is written to `tracking.chat` but never to `meta.stages`, so `buildStageRecords` keeps it out of the stage views, the progress percentage and the plan gates.
- Sessions always resume for chat (keyed `<tool>|chat`), independent of the task's opt-in `reuseSession` — a chat that forgets the previous message isn't one. `gemini` has no headless resume, so it re-sends the brief and says so.
- Everything else is inherited deliberately: the one-live-run-per-task `busy` guard, the plan gate, no commit on a failure, attach/stop.

**Two judgment calls worth your veto:**

1. **Commands are deterministic, `/`-prefixed, five of them** (`/help`, `/run`, `/agent`, `/stage add`, `/reopen`) — not natural language. The intent said "chat commands like a chatbot"; I read the mutation half as needing to be explicit, because these commands rewrite the task's flow and its git history, and `/reopen` drops commits. A classifier guessing at "maybe redo the build" is the wrong risk. Free text still goes to the agent, so the box reads as a chatbot for everything non-destructive.
2. **The existing per-stage thread view is renamed `Threads`** so `Chat` can be the new tab. Users with `bridza.taskView` = `"chat"` will land on the new view instead of the threads they had.

Scoped out and named in the spec: natural-language flow edits, `/stage remove` (removing a stage that has run *is* `/reopen`), editing past turns, chat outside a task. One new store function, `addTaskStage` — `retargetTask` only rewrites `meta.stages` when the flow itself changes, so additive stage insertion doesn't exist yet.

Add a feature to continue communicating in a chat with agents inside task details even after steps are done and you need to further improvise it.  I mean the flows are already there but it can also be changed and updated with just chat commands like a chatbot and it should be available in the task details.

Fit check — this task was filed under the "Feature" flow. The earlier stages' outputs (research, requirements, design…) are in the worktree — read them, then judge whether this really is a single "Feature" task. The pipeline's other flows: "Full product SDLC" (Vision → Requirements → Design & Architecture → Sprint Planning → Implementation → Testing → Review & Release); "Bugfix" (Reproduce → Fix → Review); "UI design" (Spec → Design); "Feature dissection" (Dissect). If it belongs in a different flow (e.g. it's a multi-task feature that must be broken down, not implemented in one go), STOP: write flow-fit.md naming the right flow and why — the earlier stages' work stays on this branch — and do NO implementation. If it fits, proceed normally.
